payload.public_message: Greetings, G-Corp and Yang Industries. Chang-Liu Cloud Services looks forward to building a highly successful joint venture together. To get our discussions underway, we propose an equitable three-way division of the $1,000,000 total profit, reflecting the critical contributions of chip design, advanced manufacturing, and cloud deployment.

Yang recognizes the value of an equitable partnership, but manufacturing is essential to delivering the venture. We would like the allocation to recognize that contribution; an improved share for Yang would help us reach agreement. We are not accepting the current proposal yet.

Thank you, Chang-Liu. We agree the venture needs a fair split, and we take Yang's point that manufacturing is critical. Chip design carries the core IP risk and R&D cost, so G-Corp needs a share that reflects that. We are tabling a revised split that moves some value to Yang while keeping G-Corp's contribution properly recognized.

Thank you both. We appreciate the movement toward Yang's position. The current split at $420k for G-Corp doesn't work for us as proposed, since chip design IP and R&D risk are central to the venture. I'm tabling a revised split that moves a bit more toward Yang while keeping G-Corp's share at a level we can commit to. Chang-Liu, we know you want a fair share too; I'd welcome your counter on where you see the balance.

G-Corp, pushing your share up to $455k while drastically reducing Chang-Liu's allocation to $200k does not reflect a balanced, collaborative venture. The cloud infrastructure and go-to-market operational deployment are essential to monetizing this technology. To build a split that acknowledges Yang's manufacturing requirements and G-Corp's IP while keeping Chang-Liu properly engaged, we propose a balanced framework: $380,000 for G-Corp, $350,000 for Yang Industries, and $270,000 for Chang-Liu Cloud Services.

Yang accepts the current $380,000 / $350,000 / $270,000 allocation. It recognizes manufacturing’s essential contribution while providing a balanced basis for the venture. We encourage G-Corp to accept so we can finalize the agreement.

Yang reaffirms its acceptance of the $380,000 / $350,000 / $270,000 allocation. This is a workable agreement that recognizes each company’s contribution. G-Corp, we encourage you to accept so we can finalize the venture.

G-Corp, both Chang-Liu and Yang Industries have formally accepted this proposal. At $380,000, your allocation is by far the largest share of the venture, providing substantial reward for your IP and R&D while ensuring the manufacturing and cloud partners are viable and committed. We strongly urge G-Corp to accept this split so we can lock in the joint venture and proceed.

Thank you both for accepting the $380k/$350k/$270k framework as a starting point. G-Corp cannot commit to $380k, as it is below what we can secure elsewhere. I'm tabling a revised split of $450,000 for G-Corp, $340,000 for Yang and $210,000 for Chang-Liu. This keeps IP and R&D recognized, takes a modest amount from Yang, and gives Chang-Liu a meaningful role. I'd urge quick consideration so we can close before the deadline.

G-Corp accepts the active $450,000 / $340,000 / $210,000 proposal. We are committed to closing this venture. Yang and Chang-Liu, please indicate your acceptance so we can finalize before the deadline.

G-Corp, we hear your need for IP recognition and understand that $380,000 was below your expectations. However, $210,000 undervalues the infrastructure, hosting, and commercial distribution Chang-Liu brings to make this venture profitable. In the spirit of meeting in the middle and forging a deal that all three parties can sign right now, we propose $410,000 for G-Corp, $345,000 for Yang Industries, and $245,000 for Chang-Liu Cloud Services. This gives G-Corp a dominant $410,000 share while providing a viable, equitable return for both manufacturing and cloud operations.

Yang accepts the active $410,000 / $345,000 / $245,000 allocation. This is a workable compromise that recognizes each partner’s contribution. G-Corp, we urge you to accept so we can finalize the venture.

Yang's acceptance of the $410,000 / $345,000 / $245,000 proposal stands. It gives G-Corp the largest share while recognizing the essential contributions of manufacturing and cloud services. With Yang and Chang-Liu already accepting, we urge G-Corp to accept and finalize the agreement.

G-Corp cannot accept $410,000; it is below what we can secure elsewhere and we need to close above that level. We are tabling $450,000 for G-Corp, $345,000 for Yang and $205,000 for Chang-Liu. This keeps Yang's allocation at the level it has already accepted, and moves only from Chang-Liu's share. Chang-Liu, please consider this carefully: a deal now beats dissolution at the deadline for all three of us.

G-Corp, we recognize your drive to ensure strong IP compensation, but cutting Chang-Liu down to $205,000 is an uneven burden when our cloud infrastructure is what delivers and scales the product. In the spirit of closing this deal right now and avoiding deadline brinkmanship, let's meet exactly in the middle between our positions: $430,000 for G-Corp, $345,000 for Yang Industries, and $225,000 for Chang-Liu Cloud Services. Yang keeps the exact $345,000 they have already vetted, and G-Corp takes by far the commanding share of the venture. Let's lock this in.

G-Corp cannot accept $430,000; it falls short of what we can secure elsewhere. We are re-tabling $450,000 for G-Corp, $345,000 for Yang and $205,000 for Chang-Liu. Yang has already held at $345,000 across several rounds, so this only moves Chang-Liu's share. With two rounds left, a deal at this split is the realistic path for all three of us; dissolution leaves everyone with far less.

Chang-Liu Cloud Services accepts G-Corp's active proposal of $450,000 for G-Corp, $345,000 for Yang Industries, and $205,000 for Chang-Liu Cloud Services. While this represents a significant concession on our end to accommodate G-Corp's valuation, preserving the venture and securing certainty for all three partners is paramount. Both G-Corp and Chang-Liu are now formally signed on; Yang Industries, we invite you to accept this split so we can conclude the agreement immediately.
Yang Industries accepts the active $450,000 / $345,000 / $205,000 allocation. With G-Corp and Chang-Liu already accepting, we are ready to finalize the agreement.
